title: Birth in Mississippi and his mother's family
summary: Blakeney gives his birth date and place and tells of his grandmother, a slave, and how his mother became a teacher and married his father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I am Andrew Blakeney, birth dated June 10, 1898, born Quitman, Mississippi. I am the son of Thomas and Anna Lucie Price Blakeney. I am the grandson of Lucie Price and Madison Price. I don't recall my paternal grandparents.

My grandmother was brought to Mississippi from Virginia by some people as a slave in her teens. Years later, she was permitted to marry the house slave by the name of Luke. Twelve children resulted from that union. My mother, Anna Lucie, was the eleventh child. My mother--the two youngest--were sent to Meridian to school by the big city just fifteen miles north of Enterprise.
One year later she went to Quitman, the county seat of Clark County to receive a license to teach. There

she met my father who was already a teacher They were married in June, 1897. I was born June 10, 1898 on a farm my father bought before he married my mother. Eight more children followed me. That ended my mother's teaching career.
